title: Apple (Malus domestica)
description: Easy to recognize when there are fruits on the tree. The leaves are spaced out pretty widely and the tree itself is often short and wide. The biggest production area is in Aomori. Other than that, apples can also be found often around Nagano and Gunma.

title: Peach (Prunus persica)
description: A shorter Prunus species. Mostly found in Fukushima, Yamanashi and Okayama.

title: Sweet Cherry (Prunus avium)
description: Sweet Cherry has longer, light green leaves for a Prunus. Almost only found in Yamagata.

title: Plantain Banana (Musa × paradisiaca)
description: Banana trees are very easy to spot. Most commonly found on the Ryukyu islands but sometimes can be found elsewhere.

title: Sour Orange (Citrus × aurantium)
description: Orange trees have short messy leaves. Easy to spot with the fruits. Mostly found in the south and a lot in Ehime.

title: Sour Orange (Citrus × aurantium)
description: Orange trees have short messy leaves. Easy to spot with the fruits. Mostly found in the south and a lot in Ehime.

title: Japanese Persimmon (Diospyros kaki)
description: Short and wide tree. The leaves are glossy and oval shaped. Mostly found in Kudoyama, Wakayama to Gojo, Nara. Also some on the Aichi Shizuoka border.

title: Wine Grape (Vitis vinifera)
description: Super recognizable especially with the setup. Mostly found in Yamanashi.

title: Olive (Olea europaea)
description: Olives have smokey-ish leaves. Basically only found on Shodoshima.

title: Konjac (Amorphophallus konjac)
description: Greenish white plant. Basically Gunma only.

title: Corn (Zea mays)
description: It's corn. Most common in Hokkaido.

title: Cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. capitata)
description: Pale green clumps when seen in the fields. More common south of Tohoku but also exists a lot in the Tokachi plains in Hokkaido.

title: Common Onion (Allium cepa)
description: Dark green rice like leaves. You can often see the onion poking out of the dirt. Most common in Kitami, Hokkaido. The second most dense spot is Awaji Island.

title: Common Onion (Allium cepa)
description: Dark green rice like leaves. You can often see the onion poking out of the dirt. Most common in Kitami, Hokkaido. The second most dense spot is Awaji Island.

title: Asian Rice (Oryza sativa)
description: Rice fields. Can be found almost everywhere that is flat. Very useful to know the distribution for Hokkaido.

title: Tea (Camelia sinensis)
description: Tea farms are recognizable by the dark green hedges planted in rows. These fans can also be found alongside them. Shizuoka is by far the biggest tea production prefecture followed by Kagoshima. Other spots include Iruma City, Suzuka City, Wazuka City, Yame City and scattered around the Miyazaki plain.

title: Soybean (Glycine max)
description: Soybeans are these bushy green plants (yellow in Autumn) with trifoliate leaves that are oval in shape. Mostly in Hokkaido.

title: Sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum)
description: Super easy to notice. Mostly on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Sugi (Cryptomeria japonica)
description: Japanese Cedar is the most commonly seen conifer and the official national tree of Japan. It is easily identified by the circular clumps of leaves on the tip of each branch. It can be found from Yakushima up to the Oshima peninsula in Hokkaido. This is especially useful in Hokkaido or on islands. Yakushima is home to giant Sugis called Yakusugi (屋久杉).

title: Hinoki Cypress (Chamaecyparis obtusa)
description: A species of cypress native to Japan. It has a reddish bark and the leaves are fan shaped. Found primarily in hilly areas of the south. Also planted a lot near tea farms as a wind breaker.

title: Hinoki Cypress (Chamaecyparis obtusa)
description: A species of cypress native to Japan. It has a reddish bark and the leaves are fan shaped. Found primarily in hilly areas of the south. Also planted a lot near tea farms as a wind breaker.

title: Sawara Cypress (Chamaecyparis pisifera)
description: It has a dark reddish brown bark and feathery leaves. Although native to Kyushu and Honshu, it is now found mostly in central Japan.

title: Nikko Fir (Abies homolepis)
description: The leaves are needle-like and flattened. Found in the mountains of central Honshu.

title: Momi Fir (Abies firma)
description: The needles seem to start growing halfway up the branches. Native to central and southern Japan, it grows at moderate altitudes and can be found all over the country.

title: Marie's Fir (Abies mariesii)
description: Has the most unique appearance of all the Japanese Firs. Also the tree that makes the Zao Snow Monsters. It grows at super high altitudes from central Honshu to northern Honshu, usually on mountain peaks.

title: Marie's Fir (Abies mariesii)
description: Has the most unique appearance of all the Japanese Firs. Also the tree that makes the Zao Snow Monsters. It grows at super high altitudes from central Honshu to northern Honshu, usually on mountain peaks.

title: Sakhalin Fir (Abies sachalinensis)
description: Pyramidal crown with these distinctly spiky looking branches with needles that kind of look like moss. Everywhere in Hokkaido.

title: Veitch's Fir (Abies veitchii)
description: Looks like a less mossier version of the Sakhalin Fir. Native to the mountains of Honshu and Shikoku.

title: Veitch's Fir (Abies veitchii)
description: Looks like a less mossier version of the Sakhalin Fir. Native to the mountains of Honshu and Shikoku.

title: Japanese Larch (Larix kaempferi)
description: The Japanese Larch is easily identifiable by the branches growing upwards with the needles often hanging downwards. It is mostly found in the mountains of central Chubu and Kanto as well as Iwate and Hokkaido.

title: Japanese Larch (Larix kaempferi)
description: The Japanese Larch is easily identifiable by the branches growing upwards with the needles often hanging downwards. It is mostly found in the mountains of central Chubu and Kanto as well as Iwate and Hokkaido.

title: Yakushima White Pine (Pinus amamiana)
description: A very rare species of White Pine. Native to the mountains of Yakushima and Tanegashima.

title: Yakushima White Pine (Pinus amamiana)
description: A very rare species of White Pine. Native to the mountains of Yakushima and Tanegashima.

title: Japanese Red Pine (Pinus densiflora)
description: A pine with reddish bark and green-brownish needles. It is very easily noticeable. It is found around mountainous regions of Japan, particularly common in Nagano and Fukushima. It can be useful to learn the clusters in other regions too.

title: Japanese Red Pine (Pinus densiflora)
description: A pine with reddish bark and green-brownish needles. It is very easily noticeable. It is found around mountainous regions of Japan, particularly common in Nagano and Fukushima. It can be useful to learn the clusters in other regions too.

title: Luchu Pine (Pinus luchuensis)
description: Has an open flat-topped crown with branches angled upwards. It is also usually smaller than other pines in Japan. Found on the Ryukyu and Tokyo Islands.

title: Japanese White Pine (Pinus parviflora)
description: A species of soft pine that has a wide, dense conical crown. Found in high elevation on Honshu and Hokkaido.

title: Japanese White Pine (Pinus parviflora)
description: A species of soft pine that has a wide, dense conical crown. Found in high elevation on Honshu and Hokkaido.

title: Japanese Black Pine (Pinus thunbergii)
description: A pine featuring a black bark with dark green needles. It is found in coastal places all the way down to Okinawa main island.

title: Japanese Black Pine (Pinus thunbergii)
description: A pine featuring a black bark with dark green needles. It is found in coastal places all the way down to Okinawa main island.

title: Glehn's Spruce (Picea glehnii)
description: Branches curve upwards slowly and look mossy from the needles. Native to Hokkaido.

title: Jezo Spruce (Picea jezoensis)
description: Branches curve more messily than Glehn’s Spruce. Mostly found on the mountains of Nagano but could be found up to Hokkaido.

title: Hiba (Thujopsis dolabrata)
description: Looks like a more furry Sugi if that even makes sense. The densest forests are in Aomori but individual trees can be found elsewhere.

title: Hiba (Thujopsis dolabrata)
description: Looks like a more furry Sugi if that even makes sense. The densest forests are in Aomori but individual trees can be found elsewhere.

title: Camphor (Camphora officinarum)
description: The canopy of the tree is rounded and puffy. The leaves have a glossy, waxy appearance up close. Can be found anywhere southern from the top of the Kanto plains.

title: Japanese Bay Tree (Machilus thunbergii)
description: It is an evergreen tree that has long leathery leaves that points upwards. On big trees, the branches grow very messily. Sometimes it produces red flowers which makes it look like it's glowing from afar. As the name suggests, it grows in coastal Japan, often southern.

title: Nanto Actinodaphne (Litsea acuminata)
description: A medium sized tree with long very dark green leaves in a circular pattern. Found in the south, particularly common in the Kii Peninsula.

title: Nanto Actinodaphne (Litsea acuminata)
description: A medium sized tree with long very dark green leaves in a circular pattern. Found in the south, particularly common in the Kii Peninsula.

title: Shirodamo (Neolitsea sericea)
description: It is a medium sized tree with long evergreen leaves in a circular pattern and produces yellow flowers. The leaves are a little more blue than Litsea. It is found mostly in the south and the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Shirodamo (Neolitsea sericea)
description: It is a medium sized tree with long evergreen leaves in a circular pattern and produces yellow flowers. The leaves are a little more blue than Litsea. It is found mostly in the south and the Ryukyu Islands.

title: False Indigo Bush (Amorpha fruticosa)
description: These shrubby mimosoid looking plants. The leaves are made up of many oval-shaped leaflets. Mostly found in the north.

title: Kudzu (Pueraria montana)
description: It is these vines with leaves that have 3 sections. Can be seen almost anywhere but Hokkaido but the west coast has large quantities of it.

title: Kudzu (Pueraria montana)
description: It is these vines with leaves that have 3 sections. Can be seen almost anywhere but Hokkaido but the west coast has large quantities of it.

title: Black Locust (Robinia pseudoacacia)
description: These trees with the oval leaflets at the ending of the branch appearing smaller and smokier. More common in the north.

title: Black Locust (Robinia pseudoacacia)
description: These trees with the oval leaflets at the ending of the branch appearing smaller and smokier. More common in the north.

title: Persian Silk Tree (Albizia julibrissin)
description: Large frond like leaves, with a dark greenish gray bark. Mostly found in the south.

title: White Leadtree (Leucaena leucocephala)
description: Looks very similar to a Mimosa but a lot smaller and greener. Found in Amami and everything Okinawa main island and below.

title: Taiwan Acacia (Acacia confusa)
description: This is a medium sized tree that has very small long leaves that grow messily. Found on the Okinawa Islands.

title: Japanese Bigleaf Magnolia (Magnolia obovata)
description: Big leaves with a wavy pattern surrounding the stem in a circular pattern. Most often found in the north.

title: Japanese Bigleaf Magnolia (Magnolia obovata)
description: Big leaves with a wavy pattern surrounding the stem in a circular pattern. Most often found in the north.

title: Erman's Birch (Betula ermanii)
description: Has a more complex branching pattern than other birches at the base. Also has a pink tilted bark. It grows on mountain tops in Honshu and Hokkaido at around 1500-2500m elevation.

title: Siberian Birch (Betula platyphylla)
description: Grows straight up with a white bark. Found in Hokkaido and high elevation places in Honshu.

title: Monarch Birch (Betula maximowicziana)
description: Has very big leaves for a birch and a grayish peeling bark. Mostly in Hokkaido but there are some occasional ones in high altitude spots in Honshu.

title: Japanese Beech (Fagus crenata)
description: It is easily identifiable from its gray bark and thin leaves. It is found from the Oshima Peninsula, including Okushiri Island, in Hokkaido, and south to the Osumi Peninsula in Kyushu in High Elevation areas. It is most commonly found in Central Honshu (Nagano) to Hokkaido.

title: Japanese Chestnut (Castanea crenata)
description: A medium sized tree.The leaves are very thin and long. Found in Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu although it seems to be seen more frequently in western Honshu.

title: Itajii Chinkapin (Castanopsis sieboldii)
description: This tree has thin long leathery leaves and a puffy canopy. It can also be spotted from far away as it has this white-goldish color in April-May coverage. Found in the south of the country.

title: Itajii Chinkapin (Castanopsis sieboldii)
description: This tree has thin long leathery leaves and a puffy canopy. It can also be spotted from far away as it has this white-goldish color in April-May coverage. Found in the south of the country.

title: Japanese Chinquapin (Castanopsis cuspidata)
description: Visually very similar to Itajii. The leaves are a bit thinner and the nut is smaller. Luckily there is no need to be able to tell them apart since they are found in the same places. Found in the south of the country.

title: Japanese Evergreen Oak (Quercus acuta)
description: It is usually bushy with dark and glossy leaves. The leaves are long and narrow. The bark is dark gray and smooth. Found in the south, mostly Kyushu.

title: Ubame Oak (Quercus phillyreoides)
description: Short leathery oval leaves. Found in the south.

title: Ring-cupped Oak (Quercus glauca)
description: An oak with glossy dark green leaves. Found in the south.

title: Ring-cupped Oak (Quercus glauca)
description: An oak with glossy dark green leaves. Found in the south.

title: Mongolian Oak (Quercus mongolica)
description: It is an oak that has gray bark and light green broad teethed leaves. Found in the north.

title: Mongolian Oak (Quercus mongolica)
description: It is an oak that has gray bark and light green broad teethed leaves. Found in the north.

title: Japanese Stone Oak (Lithocarpus edulis)
description: It has a smooth gray bark and leathery evergreen leaves with smooth edges. Found mostly on the Ryukyu and Tokyo Islands.

title: Manchurian Walnut (Juglans mandshurica)
description: Has an open ball-like crown, light gray-brown bark and huge light green feather-like leaves. Very similar to Juglans ailantifolia but more twiggy looking. Found more often in the north.

title: Manchurian Walnut (Juglans mandshurica)
description: Has an open ball-like crown, light gray-brown bark and huge light green feather-like leaves. Very similar to Juglans ailantifolia but more twiggy looking. Found more often in the north.

title: Japanese Walnut (Juglans ailantifolia)
description: Very similar to Juglans mandshurica. The leaflets are more pointed at the end and have more yellowish hairs. Japanese Walnut will often look more like a tree than Manchurian Walnut. Found mostly on Honshu.

title: Japanese Walnut (Juglans ailantifolia)
description: Very similar to Juglans mandshurica. The leaflets are more pointed at the end and have more yellowish hairs. Japanese Walnut will often look more like a tree than Manchurian Walnut. Found mostly on Honshu.

title: Beach Sheoak (Casuarina equisetifolia)
description: It has slender, drooping branchlets. The bark of the tree is grayish. Found on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Japanese Aralia (Fatsia japonica)
description: Is a shrub with a very unique spirally-arranged leaf shape that kind of looks like a Papaya. Should be found from Kanto southwards but I can't find any more of these.

title: Castor-Aralia (Kalopanax septemlobus)
description: It kind of looks like a fat maple leaf with 5-7 lobes. Mostly north of Kanto.

title: Ivy Tree (Heptapleurum heptaphyllum)
description: The leaflets are leathery and have wavy edges and are grown in a circular pattern. Found on the southern Islands.

title: Dwarf Umbrella Tree (Heptapleurum arboricola)
description: It is an evergreen shrub. The leaves are leathery in texture and have 7-9 leaflets in a circular pattern. Found in the south.

title: Japanese Cheesewood (Pittosporum tobira)
description: The leaves are oval and long in shape and leathery and shiny. Found in the south of the country including islands.

title: Giant Dogwood (Cornus controversa)
description: A very beautiful looking dogwood with layers of small white flowers. Mostly in the north.

title: Kousa Dogwood (Cornus kousa)
description: A small dogwood species with white flowers that have 4 petals. Mostly in Honshu but not Chubu.

title: Large-Leaf Dogwood (Cornus macrophylla)
description: Obviously a species of dogwood with large leaves. The flowers are made of little tiny smaller flowers similar to Cornus controversa. Will update distribution with more locs.

title: Hydrangea involucrata
description: It is a shrub with oval leaves and small blue or pink flower clusters. Found mostly in Kanto, particularly the Izu Peninsula and the Islands. The blue is Hydrangea involucrata var. Idzuensis, a variation. It is endemic to Hachijo-jima.

title: Hydrangea involucrata
description: It is a shrub with oval leaves and small blue or pink flower clusters. Found mostly in Kanto, particularly the Izu Peninsula and the Islands. The blue is Hydrangea involucrata var. Idzuensis, a variation. It is endemic to Hachijo-jima.

title: Mophead Hydrangea (Hydrangea macrophylla)
description: It is a bush that has these beautiful spherical flowers. Mostly found from Honshu to Kyushu.

title: Japanese Camellia (Camellia japonica)
description: Large glossy green leaves, best known for their flowers. Mostly found in the Kanto plains and southwards.

title: Sasanqua Camellia (Camellia sasanqua)
description: Smaller leaves than Camellia japonica. It can have flowers too but I have yet to find a high quality pano with flowers. Found mostly on the southern coast.

title: Tall Stewartia (Stewartia monadelpha)
description: A tree with a very orange bark. The leaves are dark green with serrated edges. Found on mountain tops in the coastal south.

title: Common Garcinia (Garcinia subelliptica)
description: A tree that has oval-circular leaves that are layered on top of each other. Found on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Elephant's Ear (Macaranga tanarius)
description: It is a small tree with leaves resembling Taro. Very commonly found on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Mallotus (Mallotus japonicus)
description: This plant has big heart shaped leaves. Found mostly in the south of the country.

title: Mallotus (Mallotus japonicus)
description: This plant has big heart shaped leaves. Found mostly in the south of the country.

title: Bishop Wood (Bischofia javanica)
description: A tree with reddish brown bark and small heart shaped leaves that looks like it folds through the middle. Found on the Ryukyu Islands and the Bonin Islands.

title: Bishop Wood (Bischofia javanica)
description: A tree with reddish brown bark and small heart shaped leaves that looks like it folds through the middle. Found on the Ryukyu Islands and the Bonin Islands.

title: Mongolian Poplar (Populus suaveolens)
description: A poplar that is native to northern Asia. Mostly found in Hokkaido.

title: Sakhalin Willow (Salix udensis)
description: A twiggy bush tree with very small, narrow and long leaves. Found mostly in Hokkaido.

title: Goat Willow (Salix caprea)
description: Looks like Sakhalin Willow with way wider leaves. Found from Nagano up to Hokkaido.

title: Dappled Willow (Salix integra)
description: A unique looking willow with pale green leaves arranged in opposite pairs. Mostly found from Chubu to Tohoku.

title: Salix sieboldiana
description: A willow with leaves more rounded and short than the other willow species. Found in Chugoku, Shikoku and Kyushu.

title: Sea Hibiscus (Hibiscus tiliaceus)
description: It has big heart shaped leaves. Found on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Sea Hibiscus (Hibiscus tiliaceus)
description: It has big heart shaped leaves. Found on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Chinese Hibiscus (Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis)
description: Red hibiscus. It is an artificial hybrid. Found on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Chinese Hibiscus (Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis)
description: Red hibiscus. It is an artificial hybrid. Found on the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Beach Naupaka (Scaevola taccada)
description: It is a large bush with light green leathery leaves that mostly point upwards. Sometimes it can have white flowers. It is found on the Ryukyu Islands and the Bonin Islands.

title: Beach Naupaka (Scaevola taccada)
description: It is a large bush with light green leathery leaves that mostly point upwards. Sometimes it can have white flowers. It is found on the Ryukyu Islands and the Bonin Islands.

title: Annual Fleabane (Erigeron annuus)
description: Tiny white flowers grown in bunches. Found a little bit more commonly in the north.

title: Annual Fleabane (Erigeron annuus)
description: Tiny white flowers grown in bunches. Found a little bit more commonly in the north.

title: Tall Goldenrod (Solidago altissima)
description: A very unique looking plant with a yellow cone shaped flower. Found almost everywhere in open fields except in northern Tohoku.

title: Japanese Mugwort (Artemisia princeps)
description: A small plant species that has sharp looking leaves. Mostly in the north.

title: Japanese Mugwort (Artemisia princeps)
description: A small plant species that has sharp looking leaves. Mostly in the north.

title: Oxeye Daisy (Leucanthemum vulgare)
description: Looks like a big fleabane. Has white petals with yellow centers. Mostly found in the north although pretty rare.

title: Hairy Beggarticks (Bidens pilosa)
description: It is these tiny white and yellow flowers with oval petals. It is found in southern Kyushu and the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Giant Butterbur (Petasites japonicus)
description: Also known as Hokkaido Cabbage, it is a type of Butterbur that is native to Japan. It is easily recognizable by the circular leaf. It is found in cold areas throughout Japan which includes high elevation areas and the cold north. The blue is Petasites japonicus ssp. giganteus which is the giant variant found mostly in Hokkaido. Also there is an area on the Oshima peninsula where these seem to be more rare.

title: Leopard Plant (Farfugium japonicum)
description: It looks like a dark green version of Petasites japonicus but feels more leathery and firm. Sometimes it can have yellow flowers on top. Most of it is found in Kyushu and the surrounding areas down to the main Okinawa Island so it is a really good indication if you suspect that you are in Kyushu. Additionally it is found in southern Mie and the Tokyo Islands.

title: Cutleaf Coneflower (Rudbeckia laciniata)
description: These are flowers with yellow petals and black in the center. Mostly found in the fields of Hokkaido.

title: Cutleaf Coneflower (Rudbeckia laciniata)
description: These are flowers with yellow petals and black in the center. Mostly found in the fields of Hokkaido.

title: Common Sunflower (Helianthus annuus)
description: It’s a sunflower. Very rare to find but mostly in flat areas.

title: Chokai Azami (Cirsium chokaiense)
description: This is a species of Plume Thistle that is endemic to the high elevation areas of Mount Chokai. It grows on open grasslands in the alpine zone and can reach 50-150 cm in height. Endemic to Mount Chokai.

title: Giant Knotweed (Reynoutria sachalinensis)
description: A species of Knotweed with very big leaves. Found in northern Tohoku and Hokkaido.

title: Japanese Hops (Humulus scandens)
description: It is a star shaped light green shrub. Mostly found in Tohoku but can be found elsewhere.

title: Japanese Fig (Ficus erecta)
description: It is a small tree that can be a bit hard to spot. It is found alongside streams. It produces small, sweet fruits. It is found from southern Kanto down to Okinawa.

title: Hauili Fig Tree (Ficus septica)
description: A medium sized tree with oval leaves. Only found on the Okinawa Islands.

title: Common Red-stem Fig (Ficus variegata)
description: Has dark green oval leaves with a red tinted bark. Only found on Ishigaki and Iriomote.

title: Loquat (Eriobotrya japonica)
description: A kind of unique looking plant with leathery green oval leaves that grows in a circular pattern but droops downwards. It grows mostly in southern Japan down to Okinawa main island.

title: Japanese Zelkova (Zelkova serrata)
description: It is a medium sized deciduous tree. It is characterized by a short trunk dividing into many upright and erect spreading stems forming a broad, round-topped head. The leaves are ovate to oblong-ovate with serrated or crenate margins. Mostly found in Chubu-Tohoku but it can be found elsewhere too.

title: Akaso (Boehmeria silvestrii)
description: It is a false nettle species that has 3 to 5 elongated tips with the longest one in the middle. It is very similar to Boehmeria platanifolia but it is smaller. Mostly found on the west side of Tohoku.

title: Sycamore-Leaf False Nettle (Boehmeria platanifolia)
description: Very similar to Boehmeria silvestrii. The leaves are wider and broader than Boehmeria silvestrii. A lot is found in the northwest but can also be found elsewhere.

title: Sycamore-Leaf False Nettle (Boehmeria platanifolia)
description: Very similar to Boehmeria silvestrii. The leaves are wider and broader than Boehmeria silvestrii. A lot is found in the northwest but can also be found elsewhere.

title: Siebold's False Nettle (Boehmeria sieboldiana)
description: A false nettle with large oval leaves with sharp serrated edges. Found in the south.

title: Ramie (Boehmeria nivea)
description: It has oval leaves with serrated edges that are sometimes more circular. Found in the south.

title: Redneck Rhody (Daphniphyllum macropodum)
description: It is a small tree with long leaves in a circular pattern. The stalks of the leaves are purple-reddish. It is mostly found on the southern coast down to the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Redneck Rhody (Daphniphyllum macropodum)
description: It is a small tree with long leaves in a circular pattern. The stalks of the leaves are purple-reddish. It is mostly found on the southern coast down to the Ryukyu Islands.

title: Japanese Horse-Chestnut (Aesculus turbinata)
